title: Signal stitching workflow and 24h triage timeline
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact, pragmatic workflow for stitching together telemetry when a performance regression alert fires. Goal is to get to an actionable hypothesis within 4h and a remediation plan within 24h. It covers dashboards to look at, how to align canary-vs-prod snapshots, quick bisect heuristics, and lightweight profiling commands to pinpoint bottlenecks.

Scope & assumptions:
- Applies to model-serving regressions: increased p95/p99 latency, CPU/GPU saturation, throughput drop, or token-level cost spikes.
- We assume traces, Prometheus metrics, per-route request logs, and canary snapshots are being recorded.
- This is a working checklist: copy to incident channel and iterate.

Quick 0-15m: initial signal capture (first responder)
- Record alert metadata: alert id, start time, affected routes/models, thresholds that crossed. Paste to incident thread.
- Minimal triage: confirm scope (single region? single model? single route?).
- Snapshot requirements: capture a 30m window before and after the alert start (t0-30m -> t0+30m). Create short-lived retention on these raw logs.
- Set async: page SRE and on-call runtime eng.

0-60m: surface high-level deltas
- Dashboards to open (ordered):
  1) global-serving-overview: p50/p95/p99 latency by model and route (stacked)
  2) resource-health: GPU util, GPU mem, host mem, CPU steal, IO wait by host pool
  3) kvcache-eviction-rate and hit-rate by model shard
  4) batching-stats: average batch size, batch latency, batch queue-time
  5) routing-fallbacks: requests routed to fallback/cheaper models (count/time)
  6) error-rates & retried-requests (5xx, 429)
  7) canary-vs-prod-traces: example end-to-end traces side-by-side
- Quick checks: is the regression latency correlated with increased GPU utilization or decreased batch sizes?
- If GPU mem pressure is high and p99 jumps, suspect kv-cache churn or larger sequence lengths in input distribution.

Signal-stitching checklist (what to compare)
- Traffic composition: token count distribution, tokenization change (new / longer prompts), attachment sizes.
- Input entropy: fraction of requests with tool-calling or function API (more tokens per request).
- Model variant mismatch: verify that canary and prod are running identical model hashes and quantization profiles.
- Serving config drift: compare batcher config, kv-cache TTLs, compilation flags between canary and prod.
- Dependency changes: new lib build (cuda/cuDNN/ML kernel), changed kernel selection, or driver updates.

Bisect heuristics (fast, low-blast)
- Binary divide by time: If regression started at T, roll timeline back in days/hours to find first exposure. Use automated snapshot diffs (p95 by model per 1-hour bucket).
- Traffic-split bisect: if we can replicate a production traffic split to a canary population, flip small percentages to isolate.
- Canary config swap test: swap only the batcher config between prod and canary (or model weights) to see which dimension reproduces.
- Dependency toggle: if a kernel or system lib changed recently, revert that on a single canary node group and measure.

Profiling quick commands (copy/paste)
- flamegraph collection (node with affected process):
  sudo perf record -F 99 -p $(pidof runtime-host) -g -- sleep 30 && sudo perf script > out.perf && ./stackcollapse-perf.pl out.perf > out.folded && ./flamegraph.pl out.folded > flame.svg
- torch/CUDA mem profiling (for GPU):
  export TORCH_USE_CUDA_MEMORY_STATISTICS=1
  python -m scripts/single_trace_profile.py --trace-id <trace> --output /tmp/gpu-profile.json
- microbench model forward step (deterministic):
  python tools/mini_bench.py --model /models/foo:v3 --batch 1 --seq 2048 --iter 100 --device cuda:0
- batcher queue histogram (PromQL):
  histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(batcher_queue_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model))
- kv-cache eviction rate (PromQL):
  increase(kv_cache_evictions_total[30m]) / increase(kv_cache_hits_total[30m])

Canary-vs-Prod snapshot alignment (how to make apples->apples)
- Sampling: use the same random seed and request IDs for both environments. Pull 500 representative request bodies from pre-alert window and replay through canary and prod with identical concurrency and timing.
- Deterministic replay tool: use replayer/traffic_replay with --preserve-timestamps and --tokenizer-fingerprint to ensure tokenization parity.
- Compare outputs: p50/p95 latency distributions, GPU kernels called (nvprof logs), batch size histograms. Create a single comparison chart in BigQuery:
  SELECT bucket, SUM(prod_count) prod, SUM(canary_count) canary FROM perf_snapshots WHERE window = 't0' GROUP BY bucket

Decision matrix (when to rollback, when to mitigate)
- Rollback if: full-production regression and canary unaffected OR immediate SLO breach with no partial mitigations and root cause points to recent deploy (config or model).
- Mitigate if: partial or localized regressions where traffic shaping, rate-limiting, or increasing batch timeout reduces SLO breach and gives time to bisect.
- Short-term patch: reduce request concurrency to the affected pool, increase KV cache TTL, or fail-fast on largest payloads.

Postmortem checklist (within 24–72h)
- Capture: traces, full perf profiles, kernel-level logs, replay corpus.
- Root cause hypothesis and evidence table (metric + artifact proving link).
- Small experiments to confirm (config swap, revert, microbench).
- Action items: automated canary checks (traffic parity tests), dashboard alert tuning (add token-count dimension), rollout policy changes.
- Lessons learned: add a synthetic that exercises a long sequence + tool-calling path.

Notes & gotchas
- Tokenization drift: small prompt text changes can create large token-count distribution shifts; always compare tokenizer fingerprints.
- Batchers are non-linear: small changes in median batch size can amplify p99 effects due to head-of-line blocking.
- GPU kernels may hide latency: a kernel fallback (FP16 -> FP32) can be catastrophic; check kernel-selection logs in model-compiler metadata.

Appendix: quick PromQL & SQL snippets
- Average batch size by model: sum(rate(batcher_queued_tokens[5m])) / sum(rate(batcher_requests[5m])) by (model)
- p99 latency delta (BigQuery style):
  SELECT model, quantiles[OFFSET(99)] as p99 FROM TABLE(QUANTILE_DISC(0.01, latency_ms) OVER (PARTITION BY model)) WHERE window = 't0'

Who to call
- oncall-eng-serving-runtime: @oncall-serving (SRE pager)
- profiling lead: Marcus Nguyen
- model-serving owner for product models: Priya Shah

End notes
- This is intended as a living scratchplaybook. If you use a step that helps, add it here (short paragraph) and link the artifact. The most useful diffs we get are the ones that connect a single metric delta to a reproducible, small config change.
